relations.subject: capella:data-api
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - camelCase verb phrase; no existing predicate captures 'X authenticates using credential scheme Y'. Directly confirms the hypothesis: the Data API's own docs state it reuses the same cluster-access-credential model as the statement pages, not a separate API-key mechanism.
relations.evidence: The Data API uses cluster access credentials for authentication and authorization. The access privileges specified for the cluster access credential determine the buckets, scopes, and collections that a client can access via the Data API. To authenticate a Data API call, you must pass the cluster access credentials as the username and password, using HTTP Basic authentication.

notable_absence.finding: The Data API's own introduction page never uses the words 'Basic' or 'Advanced' when describing its authentication model - it only says 'cluster access credentials' generically, and that access privileges on that credential determine bucket/scope/collection access. None of the 11 files in this batch mention the Basic/Advanced credential-type dichotomy by name, even though data-api-start.md's Management API example creates a cluster user with a privilege list ("privileges": ["data_writer"]) that is a third, KV-style privilege vocabulary distinct from both the Basic/Advanced enum and the capella:capella-basic-access-*/capella-advanced-access-* named query privileges seen from the statement side. This suggests the Data API is documented as sitting on top of the same underlying cluster-access-credential mechanism, but its own docs never surface the Basic/Advanced terminology that statement pages use to describe gating.

cross_component_finding: This page (the Data API's own intro) confirms rather than extends the access-surface findings from the statement side in one respect and diverges in another. Confirms: authentication is exactly the credential-type model already promoted in the registry (cluster access credentials via HTTP Basic auth) - not a separate API-key or OAuth mechanism. This is the same credential object that Management API calls (data-api-start.md, data-api-private-aws.md, data-api-private-azure.md) authenticate against using a completely different mechanism: a Bearer token API key secret ($apiKeySecret) used only to configure/enable the Data API itself, never to call it. So there are two distinct auth axes on the same feature: Bearer-token API keys to manage the Data API (Management API), and Basic-auth cluster access credentials to use the Data API (Data API proper) - worth flagging for reconciliation as a possibly-new axis, managementPlaneCredential vs. dataPlaneCredential, since the existing cluster-access-credential-type concept only covers the latter.
cross_product_finding: Passthrough Query Service endpoints explicitly forbid one class of operation that the statement pages gate by access surface: 'Managing and administrating the Query Service is not supported' via the Data API passthrough, and Search passthrough similarly restricts to only Full-Text Search queries and Vector Search queries ('Other search requests are not supported'). This is new information not visible from the statement side: the statement pages describe incompatibleWithAccessSurface as excluding entire statement families (transactions, USING AI) from the Data API, but this page reveals the Data API also excludes entire *categories of administration* regardless of statement, which is a broader/different-shaped restriction than the per-statement one found previously.
